title: Count the flavors
scenario: The ice-cream counter took five scoops. How many DIFFERENT flavors were ordered?

intro.job: The ice-cream counter took five scoops. How many DIFFERENT flavors were ordered?

idea.rule: len(flavors) counts every copy — len(set(flavors)) counts each one once.
idea.detail: set(some_list) builds a set: every value goes in, but a value that's already there is quietly dropped. So len(set(...)) counts how many DIFFERENT values there are. len(some_list) counts every entry, twins included.

model_restatement: Count how many different flavors are on the list, ignoring repeats.

clarify.question: Could the same flavor be spelled differently?
clarify.answer: No — today the flavors are clean and lowercase.

clarify.question: Do you want the flavors, or just how many?

clarify_fallback: Good question — assume the simple case.
blueprint: Count the flavors on the list and print the number.

checkpoints.prompt: With the fix — after line 1, what is kinds?

why_line: len(flavors) counts every scoop, so mint is counted three times — 5, not 3.

explain.rule: len(flavors) is a headcount at the counter that counts mint every time it appears — three mints, three ticks.
explain.bridge: So what could you put the flavors into that keeps only one of each?

fix.rule: set(flavors) throws out the twins first; len then counts what's left — one per flavor.

alternatives.note: The long way, with a list — slower on big lists, same answer.

hints: How many times does mint appear?
len counts every entry. You want each flavor once.

follow_up.prompt: Three scoops, one flavor: ['choc', 'choc', 'choc'] — how many kinds?
follow_up.fix_hint: Nothing to change — three chocs are still one flavor.

one_liner: len(flavors) counts every copy — len(set(flavors)) counts each one once.
